summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and decompensated cirrhosis was admitted for recurrent fever and right upper quadrant pain, similar to prior cholangitis episodes. She spiked fevers up to 102.5 but remained clinically stable without signs of sepsis. Blood cultures were repeatedly negative, imaging showed no biliary obstruction, and inflammatory markers were elevated without a clear infectious source. Antibiotics were withheld, and she became afebrile within 48 hours. The fever of unknown origin may be related to underlying PSC or an immune-mediated process, with an elevated rheumatoid factor prompting rheumatology follow-up. She continued home medications for liver support and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid empiric antibiotics in the future without hepatology consultation.
